title: Follow Anthropic's Actions, Not It's Rhetoric: 5 AI Stocks to Benefit From Anthropic's $517 Billion in Compute Commitments
excerpt: These companies are set to benefit from Anthropic's massive AI infrastructure spending.
content_html:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently published an essay calling for frontier AI labs to slow their development. The worry is that AI could eventually become dangerous without proper safeguards. Movies like The Terminator certainly show what a worst-case scenario could look like.

However, the company's actions tell a much different story. According to technology publication The Information, over the past 11 months through the end of August, Anthropic agreed to spend a whopping $517 billion on computing power. That's well above the $180 billion in commitments it had previously disclosed.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Let's look at five AI stocks set to benefit from this spending.

Nvidia

Nvidia's (NASDAQ: NVDA) graphics processing units (GPUs) remain the primary chips powering AI workloads, so the more money a company like Anthropic spends on AI infrastructure, the more Nvidia benefits. Nvidia remains the dominant player in AI model training, as most foundational AI code was written on its CUDA software platform and optimized for its GPUs. Meanwhile, with its "acquisition" of Groq, it has established itself as an important player in inference.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently forecast that AI infrastructure spending would climb to between $3 trillion and $4 trillion by 2030, so the chip giant clearly sees no slowdown in spending, despite Anthropic's recent call for frontier labs to slow the pace of development. Meanwhile, it has been reported that Nvidia could invest up to $10 billion into the frontier lab as an anchor investor in its IPO.

AMD

Nvidia's GPUs aren't the only chips Anthropic is using in its AI infrastructure build-out. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) agreed to invest up to $5 billion in the company, while Anthropic will buy AMD's Helios rack-scale system to run inference.

Helios includes both AMD's new Instinct GPUs and its central processing units (CPUs). The two companies will also work together on Anthropic's Claude model to optimize workloads for its GPUs and improve ROCm software development.

As part of the deal, Anthropic will deploy up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's GPUs, with the rollout beginning in 2027. This follows two other large GPU deals for inference that AMD has made with OpenAI and Meta Platforms.

Alphabet and Broadcom
